I will keep my farm steady and practical this year. I have 13.1 mu and well irrigation, so I will still put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my farm and the crop pair I know best after 40 years. My family has seven people, but some work off-farm, so I do not want a plan that is too scattered or too labor-heavy. I will keep 8 mu in wheat-maize, because grain is the safest base for my household and irrigation helps me hold yield. I will put 3 mu into cotton because it brings cash, but I will not expand it too much because it takes more field watching and more pest control. I will plant 2.1 mu of mungbean because it is simpler, needs less fertilizer, and helps me spread risk if one crop does poorly. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps me get steadier yield, and I will not push fertilizer or irrigation too hard. I want a plan that I can manage reliably, with stable output and work I can finish on time.
